authors: S. Natha, M. Leghari, M. A. Rajput, S. S. Zia, J. Shabir
title: A Systematic Review of Anomaly Detection Using Machine and Deep Learning Techniques
venue: Quaid-e-Awam University Research Journal of Engineering Science & Technology (QUEST Research Journal)
one_line: A two-stage systematic review (2019-2021) of machine and deep learning techniques for anomaly detection, surveying methods, application domains, datasets, performance metrics, and open challenges.
problem: Anomaly detection (identifying data instances/events that deviate from expected behavior) is challenging due to limited anomalous data, ground-truth scarcity, environmental variability, and noisy/complex datasets. The paper addresses the need for a comprehensive, up-to-date review consolidating ML and DL anomaly detection techniques, their strengths/weaknesses, accuracy metrics, datasets, and application domains across 2019-2021.
methods: Systematic literature review organized in two stages: (1) a search strategy across Google Scholar, Elsevier, Springer, ACM Digital Library, and IEEE Xplore using the term 'Anomaly detection' refined with Boolean operators; (2) answering study questions. Reviews ML methods (k-NN, SVM/one-class SVM, decision trees, random forests, swarm intelligence, neural networks) and DL methods (CNN, LSTM/autoencoder, GAN, attention networks, hierarchical temporal memory, multi-model approaches). Categorizes anomalies into point, contextual, and collective. Tabulates each work's strengths/weaknesses (Table 1) and datasets/metrics/results (Table 2).
key_findings: A large share of surveyed anomaly-detection works target the surveillance domain; many use real-world datasets for training/testing.
Deep learning (CNN, LSTM/autoencoder, GAN, attention) has driven major advances over classical statistical and ML methods, especially for high-dimensional, temporal, and spatial data.

Each technique has clear trade-offs: e.g., random forests and Adaboost are computationally expensive and noise-sensitive; one-class SVM underfits with noisy data or when features exceed training samples; unsupervised methods (e.g., HTM) yield lower accuracy.
Khokhlov et al. demonstrate LSTM-based anomaly detection of complex threats on mobile/Android devices in monitored data streams, though LSTM needs significant time and bandwidth.

Open challenges include input-dataset nature, data-stream/limited-memory detection, noise and data complexity, unknown nature of anomalies (lack of labels), time complexity vs. accuracy trade-off, and lack of standardized benchmark datasets.

Future directions: richer datasets covering diverse failure scenarios, cross-validation, improving detection using low-cost sensors and small datasets, global benchmark datasets, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

strengths: Broad, consolidated coverage of both classical ML and modern DL anomaly-detection techniques with explicit per-method strengths and weaknesses (Table 1).
Aggregates accuracy/precision/recall metrics and datasets across many recent (2019-2021) works in a single comparative table (Table 2), useful as a quick reference.
Clearly articulates open challenges and future directions, including resource-limited and small-dataset detection relevant to edge/mobile deployment.
Compares itself against prior surveys, clarifying its broader scope (applications, metrics, and anomaly classification together).
weaknesses: It is a review, not an empirical study; reported metrics are from cited works under heterogeneous datasets/settings, so they are not directly comparable.
Single corresponding author from a regional journal with limited indexing; some entries in tables are inconsistent (duplicated references, mismatched years, N/A values).
No taxonomy depth on privacy-preserving or on-device/edge anomaly detection beyond brief mention of resource-limited future work.
Scope deliberately restricted to 2019-2021, so it omits newer transformer/self-supervised anomaly-detection advances and does not deeply treat security/insider-threat-specific detection.
relevance: Domain 3 of SentriZK concerns on-device/lightweight AI threat and anomaly detection. This survey maps the ML/DL anomaly-detection landscape (including LSTM/autoencoder approaches and the cited Khokhlov et al. work running LSTM-based anomaly detection on Android devices), grounding SentriZK's choice of deep-learning anomaly/insider-threat detection and its identified challenges (noisy data, small datasets, limited memory/time, real-time streams) directly motivate the need for efficient, low-resource detection suitable for TensorFlow Lite on-device deployment.
